section: Inflation - types, causes, measurement (CPI, WPI, core inflation), effects and control measures

accepted.s: Who first established an inverse relationship between unemployment and wage inflation in 1958?
o: A.W. Phillips
Urjit Patel
Milton Friedman
Abhijit Sen
accepted.x: A.W. Phillips established the inverse relationship between unemployment and wage inflation in 1958.
accepted.tq: Direct recall of the economist associated with a concept and year.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Phillips curve:
1. In the short run, lower unemployment is generally associated with higher inflation.
2. In the long run, the Phillips curve is vertical according to Friedman.
3. The long-run Phillips curve implies a lasting trade-off between inflation and unemployment.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The long-run vertical curve indicates that there is no lasting trade-off between inflation and unemployment, making statement 3 false.
accepted.tq: Separate the short-run relationship from the long-run qualification.

accepted.s: The Phillips curve observed in India during 2012–2026 has been described as relatively flat primarily because:
o: The Reserve Bank of India fixes all wages
The formal workforce has complete wage flexibility
Around 92% of workers are informal and have weak wage-bargaining power
Food prices are excluded from the CPI
accepted.x: India’s relatively flat Phillips curve is linked to the large informal workforce, estimated at about 92%, whose weak wage-bargaining power prevents wages from responding strongly to output changes.
accepted.tq: Link the observed macroeconomic outcome with its structural cause.

accepted.s: Which of the following best describes the stagflation risk associated with raising interest rates when inflation is supply-driven?
o: Interest-rate hikes necessarily reduce prices without affecting output
Interest-rate hikes increase employment and eliminate supply constraints
Interest-rate hikes affect only exports and not domestic demand
Interest-rate hikes may reduce output and employment without substantially lowering inflation
accepted.x: A repo-rate increase is primarily a demand-side measure. When inflation arises from supply shocks, it may reduce output and jobs without significantly lowering prices.
accepted.tq: Apply the demand-side versus supply-side distinction to a policy scenario.

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Monetary measure — sale of securities through open market operations
Fiscal measure — release of onion buffer stocks by NCCF
Supply-side measure — increase in cash reserve ratio
Monetary measure — reduction of indirect taxes on essential goods
accepted.x: Sale of securities through open market operations is a monetary measure. Buffer-stock release is supply-side, while taxes and government spending are fiscal instruments.
accepted.tq: Classify each instrument by identifying the authority and channel through which it works.

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Fiscal policy — tightening liquidity through open market sales
Supply-side policy — releasing buffer stocks
Fiscal policy — reducing the fiscal deficit
Monetary policy — raising the repo rate
accepted.x: Tightening liquidity through open market sales is a monetary measure undertaken by the RBI, not a fiscal measure.
accepted.tq: Find the instrument placed under the wrong policy category.

accepted.s: The principal purpose of selling securities through open market operations during inflationary conditions is to:
o: Raise the minimum export price of onions
Increase liquidity in the banking system
Tighten liquidity in the banking system
Increase the fiscal deficit
accepted.x: When the RBI sells securities through OMOs, money is withdrawn from the banking system, thereby tightening liquidity and moderating demand.
accepted.tq: Identify the immediate monetary transmission channel of an instrument.

accepted.s:
With reference to supply-side measures for controlling food inflation, consider the following statements:
1. The Food Corporation of India sells wheat and rice at fixed prices under OMSS.
2. The Price Stabilisation Fund maintains buffers of pulses and onions.
3. Bharat Atta, Bharat Rice and Bharat Dal are examples of subsidised sales.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. OMSS sales by FCI, PSF buffers and subsidised Bharat-branded food sales are supply-side responses to food inflation.
accepted.tq: Use the common policy objective to verify all three supply-side measures.

accepted.s: Bharat Chana Dal was introduced in July 2023 at which price?
o: ₹70 per kg
₹50 per kg
₹60 per kg
₹80 per kg
accepted.x: Bharat Chana Dal was introduced in July 2023 at ₹60 per kilogram.
accepted.tq: Recall the exact price attached to a subsidised anti-inflation measure.

accepted.s: Which institution or institutions were involved in releasing onion stocks from the Price Stabilisation Fund buffer?
o: FCI and RBI
SEBI and NABARD
NCCF and NAFED
NITI Aayog and CCI
accepted.x: NCCF and NAFED released 47,786 metric tonnes of onion from the PSF buffer up to 8 October 2025.
accepted.tq: Match the operational agencies with the supply-side intervention.

accepted.s: How much onion was released from the Price Stabilisation Fund buffer by NCCF and NAFED up to 8 October 2025?
accepted.x: The quantity released from the PSF onion buffer was 47,786 metric tonnes up to 8 October 2025.
accepted.tq: Test the exact quantity using closely spaced numerical distractors.

accepted.s: Subsidised sales of Bharat Atta, Bharat Rice and Bharat Dal are made through which combination of agencies?
o: CACP, SEBI and NITI Aayog
FCI, RBI and NABARD
DGFT, APEDA and EXIM Bank
NAFED, NCCF and Kendriya Bhandar
accepted.x: These subsidised food products are sold through NAFED, NCCF and Kendriya Bhandar.
accepted.tq: Recall the distribution agencies rather than the producing authority.

accepted.s:
Arrange the following developments relating to onion trade policy in chronological order:
A. Onion export ban was lifted with a 40% export duty and a US$550 minimum export price.
B. Minimum export price was removed and export duty was reduced to 20%.
C. Bharat Chana Dal was introduced.

Select the correct sequence.
o: C, A, B
A, C, B
B, A, C
C, B, A
accepted.x: Bharat Chana Dal was introduced in July 2023, the onion export ban was lifted on 4 May 2024, and the MEP was removed with duty reduced on 13 September 2024.
accepted.tq: Place the dated policy changes first and then verify the sequence.

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding onion export policy is correct?
o: The export ban was lifted on 4 May 2024 with a 40% duty and a US$550 MEP; on 13 September 2024 the MEP was removed and duty reduced to 20%.
The export ban was lifted on 4 May 2024 with a 20% duty and no MEP; on 13 September 2024 duty was raised to 40%.
The export ban continued after September 2024, but the MEP was reduced to US$550.
The export ban was lifted in September 2024 with a 40% duty, followed by restoration of the ban in October 2024.
accepted.x: The ban was lifted on 4 May 2024 subject to a 40% duty and a US$550 MEP. On 13 September 2024, the MEP was removed and the duty was reduced to 20%.
accepted.tq: Track a policy change by matching both dates and successive conditions.

accepted.s: In Andhra Pradesh, the State-level Price Monitoring Committee for essential commodities is headed by the:
o: Chairman of the State Public Service Commission
Chief Secretary
Finance Minister
Chief Commissioner of Land Administration
accepted.x: The Andhra Pradesh State-level Price Monitoring Committee is headed by the Chief Secretary.
accepted.tq: Identify the senior administrative authority associated with the monitoring mechanism.

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about price monitoring in Andhra Pradesh is correct?
o: DES monitors eight essential commodities annually, with rice and wheat added in February 2025.
The RBI monitors eight essential commodities daily in Andhra Pradesh.
DES monitors eight essential commodities daily, with groundnut oil and palm oil added in February 2025.
DES monitors only agricultural exports and does not monitor edible oils.
accepted.x: The Directorate of Economics and Statistics monitors eight essential commodities daily. Groundnut oil and palm oil were added in February 2025.
accepted.tq: Test the agency, frequency and newly added items together.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly identifies the limitation of using the repo rate to control inflation?
o: It is a supply-side tool and cannot affect demand
It is a demand-side tool and cannot directly resolve shocks such as onion prices or crude-oil prices
It directly fixes the minimum export price of agricultural commodities
It can be used only by the Union Government for reducing food stocks
accepted.x: The repo rate influences aggregate demand and liquidity, but it cannot directly remove supply shocks such as sudden increases in onion or crude-oil prices.
accepted.tq: Ask whether the policy instrument addresses the source of the shock.

accepted.s: The Urjit Patel Committee of 2014 was primarily associated with which of the following?
o: Revision of the WPI series with 2011–12 as base
Revision of the WPI series with 2004–05 as base
Introduction of inflation-indexed bonds
Monetary policy framework, CPI as nominal anchor and flexible inflation targeting
accepted.x: The Urjit Patel Committee recommended a monetary policy framework centred on CPI as the nominal anchor and flexible inflation targeting.
accepted.tq: Match the committee with its distinctive policy subject.

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Committee)
A. Urjit Patel Committee
B. Abhijit Sen Working Group
C. Saumitra Chaudhuri Working Group

List-II (Subject or base)
1. Monetary policy framework and flexible inflation targeting
2. WPI revision with 2004–05 base
3. WPI revision with 2011–12 base

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Urjit Patel was associated with the monetary policy framework; Abhijit Sen with the 2004–05 WPI revision; and Saumitra Chaudhuri with the 2011–12 WPI revision.
accepted.tq: Start with the distinctive committee-policy pair and eliminate conflicting codes.

accepted.s: Inflation-indexed bonds are securities in which:
o: Only the coupon rate is fixed permanently, irrespective of inflation
Repayment is linked exclusively to the exchange rate
The principal is linked to the stock-market index alone
The principal and/or interest is linked to an inflation index
accepted.x: In inflation-indexed bonds, the principal and/or interest payments are linked to an inflation index, protecting the investor’s real return.
accepted.tq: Use the defining contractual feature to distinguish the instrument.

accepted.s: The Reserve Bank of India issued Inflation-Indexed Bonds in:
accepted.x: The RBI issued Inflation-Indexed Bonds in 2013.
accepted.tq: Recall the introduction year using adjacent-year distractors.

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT an expected benefit of inflation-indexed bonds?
o: Expanding the investor base for government borrowing
Guaranteeing permanently lower borrowing costs regardless of inflation credibility
Moving savings away from gold
Providing investors a hedge against inflation
accepted.x: Inflation-indexed bonds provide a real-return hedge, can widen the investor base and may shift savings from gold. Cheaper government borrowing depends on credible commitment to low inflation; it is not guaranteed regardless of inflation performance.
accepted.tq: Reject the absolute claim that ignores the condition attached to cheaper borrowing.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about inflation-indexed bonds:
1. They protect investors against inflation by linking payments to an inflation index.
2. They can signal the government's commitment to maintaining low inflation.
3. They may help shift household savings away from gold.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Inflation-indexed bonds protect real returns, signal an anti-inflation commitment and offer an alternative to gold savings.
accepted.tq: Recognise the common investor, government and savings effects of the instrument.

accepted.s: In August 2026, the repo rate referred to in the monetary-policy discussion was:
accepted.x: The repo rate was stated as 5.25% in August 2026, with an October hike expected.
accepted.tq: Test a current policy rate with close percentage-point distractors.

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly represents the reported August 2026 inflation position in India?
o: CPI about 3.9% and WPI near 4.9%, driven only by manufactured goods
CPI about 9.8% and WPI near 4.8%, driven only by services
CPI about 4.8% and WPI near 1.8%, with no contribution from food
CPI about 4.8% and WPI near 9.8%, driven by fuel and food
accepted.x: The reported August 2026 figures were CPI at about 4.8% and WPI near 9.8%, with fuel and food identified as major drivers after the West Asia conflict.
accepted.tq: Keep the index labels and the direction of the comparison aligned.

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding inflation in Andhra Pradesh in May 2026 is correct?
o: AP retail inflation was 4.9%, equal to India’s 4.9%, for the fifth consecutive month.
AP retail inflation was 5.09% in urban areas and 4.61% in rural areas.
AP retail inflation was 3.9%, below India’s 4.9%.
AP retail inflation was 4.9%, above India’s 3.9%, and remained above the national rate for five consecutive months.
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh recorded retail inflation of 4.9% against India’s 3.9% in May 2026 and was above the national rate for five consecutive months.
accepted.tq: Check both the level comparison and the duration claim.

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched regarding Andhra Pradesh consumer price indices?
o: CPI-AL inflation — AP 0.81%, India 1.78%
CPI-IW centres — Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada and Kurnool
CPI-IW centres — Guntur, Vijayawada and Nellore only
CPI-AL inflation — AP 1.78%, India 0.81%
accepted.x: CPI-AL inflation was 0.81% in Andhra Pradesh against 1.78% for India. The CPI-IW centres identified were Guntur, Visakhapatnam and Nellore, with Vijayawada dropped.
accepted.tq: Match both figures and locations without swapping their jurisdictions.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the change in the CPI-Combined index?
o: Andhra Pradesh: 197.9 to 198.0; India: 192.6 to 204.9
Andhra Pradesh: 204.9 to 197.9; India: 198.0 to 192.6
Andhra Pradesh: 192.6 to 198.0; India: 197.9 to 204.9
Andhra Pradesh: 197.9 to 204.9; India: 192.6 to 198.0
accepted.x: The CPI-Combined index increased from 197.9 to 204.9 in Andhra Pradesh and from 192.6 to 198.0 in India.
accepted.tq: Keep each jurisdiction’s two-point index movement together.

accepted.s: Following the adoption of flexible inflation targeting, the average CPI inflation reportedly declined from approximately 6.8% during 2012–16 to:
accepted.x: Average CPI inflation declined from 6.8% during 2012–16 to about 4.9% after flexible inflation targeting.
accepted.tq: Test the before-and-after policy figures with nearby percentage distractors.

accepted.s: Which of the following best captures the significance of maintaining low inflation?
o: It necessarily increases the fiscal deficit and discourages foreign investment.
It benefits only exporters and has no effect on poorer households.
It protects the poor and helps anchor the rupee and foreign portfolio investment.
It eliminates all supply shocks and guarantees higher employment.
accepted.x: Low and stable inflation protects poorer households, supports confidence in the rupee and helps anchor foreign portfolio investment.
accepted.tq: Select the option that combines the distributional and macro-financial effects.

accepted.s: Which of the following concerns is associated with inflation targeting based mainly on headline CPI?
o: Headline CPI can be influenced only by fiscal policy
Inflation targeting prevents any change in interest rates
Headline CPI excludes all food and fuel shocks by definition
Most inflation shocks may be supply-driven, while monetary-policy transmission can be slow
accepted.x: A key criticism is that headline CPI may reflect supply shocks that interest rates cannot quickly resolve, while policy transmission may also be slow.
accepted.tq: Identify the policy-design criticism arising from the source and transmission of inflation.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding inflation in June–July 2026:
1. Headline CPI moved back above 4%.
2. The increase was food-led.
3. Core inflation remained stable.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: Headline CPI was reported above 4% in June–July 2026, with food as the main driver while core inflation remained stable.
accepted.tq: Combine the headline movement, principal driver and core-inflation condition.
